why: 6 of 8 check types (passive ratio, sentence/avg-length caps, paragraph length, jargon substitution, unexplained-acronym-first-use) have real, free equivalents (write-good's passive check, Vale's confirmed Acronyms rule, Vale/write-good Wordiness). Two do not: unbacked_number is this repo's own claim-discipline rule (tied to the retracted 24%-64% incident), and hidden-verb/nominalization was not found in proselint, write-good, or Vale's rule sets. Verdict: keep the two novel checks plus CI/mutate.py wiring; the rest duplicates available tooling.

alternatives.name: textstat
alternatives.covers: Readability/grade-level formulas: Flesch Reading Ease, Flesch-Kincaid Grade, SMOG, Coleman-Liau, ARI, Dale-Chall, Gunning Fog, Linsear Write, from syllable/word/sentence counts.
alternatives.gap: Computes zero of plain.py's actual checks: no passive-voice ratio, no hidden-verb/nominalization, no jargon substitution, no acronym-first-use, no unbacked-number rule, no markdown-aware code/prose split.
alternatives.cost: Free, MIT, pure Python, pip install textstat; depends on Pyphen (also pure Python, offline-cacheable).
alternatives.maturity: v0.7.13 released 2026-02-18 per PyPI (WebFetch checked); long-running, actively released.

alternatives.name: proselint
alternatives.covers: Prose style linter: weasel words, cliches, industrial jargon, redundancy, hedging, malapropisms, spelling/typography consistency.
alternatives.gap: No passive-voice check, no nominalization/hidden-verb check, no acronym-first-use check, no unbacked-number rule (its GitHub checks/ directory lists neither module, per WebFetch).
alternatives.cost: Free, BSD license, pure Python, pip install proselint.
alternatives.maturity: Actively maintained on GitHub (amperser/proselint); long-established project.

alternatives.name: write-good
alternatives.covers: Heuristic checks close to ours: passive voice, weasel words, wordy phrases, adverb overuse, 'there is/are' openers, cliches.
alternatives.gap: No nominalization/hidden-verb suffix scan, no acronym-first-use, no unbacked-number rule, no markdown-aware frontmatter/table/list extraction.
alternatives.cost: Free, Node.js/npm only; no Python port found -- adds a JS toolchain to a Python-only repo.
alternatives.maturity: Long-standing (btford/write-good); low recent-commit signal in what WebFetch returned.

alternatives.name: Vale (+ Google/Microsoft/write-good style packs)
alternatives.covers: Confirmed acronym-first-use rule, wordiness/jargon substitution, a ported write-good passive-voice style, native markdown/HTML scope-aware parsing.
alternatives.gap: No built-in nominalization/hidden-verb rule found; no unbacked-number rule; style packs need vendoring into the repo for offline CI, not fetched by default.
alternatives.cost: Free, MIT, Go binary; winget/scoop/zip install, no WSL; `vale sync` needs network unless styles vendored.
alternatives.maturity: Actively maintained (vale-cli org); widely used by doc teams per 2026 sources.

evidence: Read plain.py:1-631 (full), SKILL.md:1-129. grep 'plain\.py' -> ship-gate.yml:140-149 (live CI) and tools/audit/mutations/plain.py (mutation spec) -- active caller. Ran `python plain.py selftest`: 'all checks passed'. WebFetch confirmed textstat's PyPI page, proselint's checks/ dir, Vale's acronym-rule doc; write-good/Vale recency is WebSearch-summary only, not commit-pinned.
recheck: pip install proselint; vale sync (or vendor Google+write-good styles) then diff output against `python dot-claude/skills/explain-simply/plain.py check --json SKILL.md`; re-run plain.py selftest.
migration_loc: Delete ~380 lines (passive/jargon/acronym/length checks + their selftest); add ~150-200 lines vendored Vale YAML + CI step; keep ~250 lines (extraction, hidden_verb, unbacked_number, CLI).
what_ours_does: plain.py (630 lines) strips markdown (frontmatter/code/tables/URLs/headings), then flags sentence>25 words, avg>20 words, passive ratio (>50% gated), hidden-verb/nominalization, jargon substitutions, unexplained acronyms, and a repo-only 'unbacked_number' rule (numeral needs a matching digit in a code block). CLI + selftest wired into ship-gate.yml CI and mutate.py.
strongest_counterargument: Vale/write-good require adding a non-Python (Go/Node) toolchain and vendored style packs for offline CI; for a single maintainer, one self-contained, self-tested Python file may be less total cognitive load than composing 2-3 external tools to regain equivalent coverage, even though those tools are individually mature and free.
